hypothesis.name: Gradient-magnitude-gated tensor dimensionality with NMS skeletonization
hypothesis.statement: Horizontal gradient magnitude from the potential-field gradient tensor is the most direct fault signal; gating by the eigenvalue dimensionality index removes compact intrusions while preserving strike-extended faults; NMS skeletonization thins to width-0 for optimal DTI economics.

mechanism: Compute FFT gradient tensors for RTP magnetic and isostatic gravity fields. Extract horizontal gradient magnitude as primary edge detector. Gate by Pedersen-Rasmussen dimensionality index (near-2D = fault, near-3D = intrusion). Corroborate across both fields via geometric mean. Apply NMS skeletonization to thin to width-0 ridge crests. Output as sparse dot predictions with confidence values from the gated score surface.
non_fault_mimic: lithologic contacts and dike swarms produce similar gradient ridges
compact intrusions produce gradient signals but are filtered by dimensionality gate
survey-line striping creates linear artifacts (masked by striping detection)

holdout_dti.note: DTI vs catalogue is NOT the competition metric. The competition scores against private new-fault labels. These values are diagnostics only.
